ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in rectangle $ABCD$, $AB=6$, $BC=2$. Point $B$ is on line $l$, and the distance from point $A$ to line $l$, denoted as $AE=4$. What is the distance from point $C$ to line $l$, denoted as $CF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a rectangle,\\
it follows that $\angle ABC=90^\circ$,\\
hence $\angle ABE+\angle FBC=90^\circ$,\\
since $\angle EAB+\angle ABE=90^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle EAB=\angle FBC$,\\
also, since $\angle AEB=\angle BFC$,\\
it follows that $\triangle AEB\sim \triangle BFC$,\\
therefore $\frac{AB}{BC}=\frac{AE}{BF}$, that is, $\frac{6}{2}=\frac{4}{BF}$,\\
hence $BF=\frac{4}{3}$,\\
thus $CF=\sqrt{BC^{2}-BF^{2}}=\boxed{\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{3}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a horizontal straight line l, point B is on straight line l, and points E, B, F are also on the same straight line l. Rectangle ABCD is placed obliquely, A is directly above E, and AE is perpendicular to l; C is directly above F, and CF is perpendicular to l. In the figure, AB and BC are adjacent sides of the rectangle, therefore AB ⟂ BC. It is known that AB=6, BC=2, AE=4, and CF is required. Reasoning: Because ABCD is a rectangle, ∠ABC=90°. Also because BE and BF are both on straight line l, AE ⟂ l, and CF ⟂ l, △AEB and △BFC are both right triangles. Near point B, from AB ⟂ BC, we can get ∠ABE+∠FBC=90°; and in △AEB, ∠EAB+∠ABE=90°, so ∠EAB=∠FBC. Also ∠AEB=∠BFC=90°, therefore △AEB ∼ △BFC. According to the correspondence AB ↔ BC, AE ↔ BF, there is AB/BC = AE/BF. Substituting AB=6, BC=2, AE=4, gives 6/2 = 4/BF, so BF=4/3. Finally, in right triangle BCF, BC=2 is the hypotenuse, BF=4/3, therefore CF=sqrt(BC^2-BF^2)=sqrt(4-16/9)=sqrt(20/9)=2√5/3.
